gap: No result ChatGPT got states that SoundGuys' standardized battery test (music looped at 80 dB from 1 m) got only 7 h 03 min from the Bose SoundLink Flex (2nd Gen), against the 12 hours Bose claims and ChatGPT repeated.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited pages, jabra.com's Speak2 55 overview and bose.com's SoundLink Flex (2nd Gen) page, and against the uncited Jabra tech sheets and Bose support spec page in the results. Both cited pages give only maker claims: Jabra says up to 12 h wireless and 85 dB SPL peak at 0.5 m, and Bose says up to 12 h at 50% volume. Neither page has a third-party measurement. Neither page says how much the battery falls short at real listening levels, and neither has an independent view of call performance.
decides: ChatGPT picked the Bose Flex 2 for music plus calls, and the pick still holds. Headphonecheck's Sven Opitz rated its call performance 'very good' and reached 30 m line-of-sight range against Bose's quoted 9 m. But the page should say to expect about 7 hours at 80 dB, not 12. In a battery-weighted comparison that favours the Tribit StormBox Micro 3, which Dealectric lists, on its 24 h claim at 50% volume. I could not open a measured hour figure for the Micro 3, so that is a claim against a measurement. The research also rules out the JBL Clip 5, which Dealectric lists: SoundGuys says it has no microphone, so it cannot take calls and should not appear on this page. For the Jabra Speak2 55, PCQuest measured 5 h 24 min of music at 100% volume. That is a worst-case music test, not the talk time Jabra quotes, so it does not undercut its role as the meetings pick.
